Sparkle #8 unfolds in CAM’s Performance Space among Evans’s exhibition, welcoming audiences to interact directly with Evans. (Cash Rules Everything Around Me) to St. Louis. Part block party and part opportunity fair, C.R.E.A.M. connects community members—such as students, job seekers, queer activists, artists, and people affected by the justice system—with free resources and supportive services. Whether you, someone you love, or members of your community are looking for helpful paths forward, come to the C.R.E.A.M. Fair for a joyful communal space centered on care, creativity, and collective support. Bright, comfortable clothes are encouraged—no suits allowed! Schedule 10:00 am / The C.R.E.A.M. Fair opens with the following offerings: • Engage in an interactive art activity with Freedom Arts & Education Center • Discover the cultural resources of 4theVille, Show Me The World, and The Black Rep • Learn how Keyway Center for Diversion & Reentry offers assistance on housing stability, financial security, emotional wellness, and community reengagement • Explore Mission: St. Louis’s Beyond Jobs program for individuals seeking meaningful employment, career advancement, and opportunities to build greater stability • Sign up with St. Louis Public Library to get a library card and access to Tech Connect services, including website development, resume writing, and Creative Experience (recording rooms, 3D printers, laser cutters, digital creative software, and more!) • Meet with admissions representatives from Harris-Stowe State University, Ranken Technical College, and Webster University • Access health resources from the St. Louis City Health Department 10:00–11:30 am / Play Date drop-in art activity 11:00 am / Performance by Harris Stowe State University Honeycombs and The Swarm Drumline 11:30 am–2:00 pm / Complimentary food 12:00–12:30 pm / Resume-writing and job-search workshop with St. Louis Public Library 12:00–1:00 pm / Free headshots with Tyler Small 12:30 pm / Art + Wellness with Nico Marie 1:00 pm / Panel Discussion with Chloe Bass and Hayveyah McGowan, moderated by Ayana Evans 2:00 pm / Step performance by Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity Inc. 2:30 pm / Closing Remarks This event is free and open to the public. event.title: Book Talk with Sonny Buttar, author of Daughters of Rosebud
event.venue_json: {"id":9986,"global_id":"www.grandcenter.org?id=9986","venue":"High Low","address":"3301 Washington Ave.","city":"St. Louis","country":"United States","state":"MO","website":"http://highlowstl.com/","url":"https://www.grandcenter.org/venue/high-low/","show_map":false,"show_map_link":true}
event.description: Left Bank Books and the Left Bank Books Foundation are delighted to present St. Louisan Sonny Buttar’s debut novel, The Daughters of Rosebud (2026). Join us at High Low Literary Arts Cafe to welcome Sonny Buttar for a presentation and book signing, free and open to the public. Sonny will be in conversation with St. Louis author and Board Chair of Kimbilio for Black Fiction, David Haynes. The Daughters of Rosebud is a powerful exploration of sisterhood, family loyalty, and the courage it takes to heal. Teacher Salma Chaudhry lives a quiet life, avoiding all attachments. Growing up in small-town Rosebud, Salma and her older sister Asma were inseparable, but amid their mother’s decline and their parents’ rigid expectations, Asma makes a choice that tears the family apart. The fallout changes everything–and forces Salma to choose between her sister and her parents. Salma has spent years trying to forget. But as she recollects her past and considers reconciliation with her father, a young student opens a surprising connection to Asma’s past. In finally facing her history, Salma finds the bravery to love and hope again.

event.description: Travel from Estonia to the German Rhineland as conductor Kristiina Poska makes her SLSO debut in a concert that celebrates a variety of European folk music. Poska introduces us to the musical shapeshifting of a new composition by fellow Estonian, Ülo Krigul, and rising-star pianist Marie-Ange Nguci shines in Mozart’s sweet and playful Piano Concerto No. 21. Robert Schumann’s Third Symphony emphasizes the vibrant culture along the Rhine River in Germany, re-imagining folk dances, bucolic scenes, and the grandeur of a cathedral.

event.title: Latin Nights: Manos PanAmerica
event.venue_json: {"id":31216,"global_id":"www.grandcenter.org?id=31216","venue":"The Key Burger Bar & Boogie","address":"3225 Olive Street","city":"St. Louis","country":"United States","state":"MO","zip":"63103","website":"https://www.thekeystl.com/","url":"https://www.grandcenter.org/venue/the-key-burger-bar-boogie/","show_map":false,"show_map_link":true}
event.description: Manos PanAmerica is a Latin and North American fusion band that aims to reduce the gap between Latin and North America by playing its original and cover songs. It originated in 2023 in Saint Louis, Missouri, and is one of the few music projects in the city that incorporates various Latin genres and instruments into its performances. Some of the genres Manos PanAmerica covers include cachimbos, cumbia, bossa nova, joropos, boleros, huaynos, bailecitos, rancheras, corridos, and salsa. Some of the instruments included in Manos PanAmerica are the charango, Colombian tiple, Venezuelan cuatro, quena, and zampoñas, among others.

event.description: An eclectic group of six mid-pubescents vie for the spelling championship of a lifetime. While candidly disclosing hilarious and touching stories from their home lives, the tweens spell their way through a series of (potentially made-up) words, hoping never to hear the soul-crushing, pout-inducing, life un-affirming “ding” of the bell that signals a spelling mistake. Six spellers enter; one speller leaves a champion!
